questions.q_en: The development of a fruit without fertilization is called ________.
questions.solution_en: Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilization. The fruit resembles a normally produced fruit but is seedless. Varieties of the pineapple, banana, cucumber, grape, orange, grapefruit, persimmon, and breadfruit exemplify naturally occurring parthenocarpy.
questions.solution_hi: पार्थेनोकार्पी निषेचन के बिना फल का विकास है। फल सामान्य रूप से उत्पादित फल जैसा दिखता है परंतु बीजरहित होता है। अनानास, केला, खीरा, अंगूर, संतरा, चकोतरा व ब्रेडफ्रूट की किस्में प्राकृतिक रूप से होने वाली पार्थेनोकार्पी का उदाहरण हैं।

questions.q_en:
Match the terms in column A with their respective properties in column B.

COLUMN ACOLUMN B
i. Glucosea. Intermediate substance in breakdown of glucose
ii. Yeastb. Glucose is converted into Pyruvic acid
iii. Glycolysisc. Use nutrients for fermentation process
iv. Pyruvic acidd. Best organic substrate for respiration
questions.solution_en:
Glucose → d (Best organic substrate for respiration)

· Glucose is the primary energy source for cellular respiration, making it the best organic substrate.

Yeast → c (Uses nutrients for fermentation process)

· Yeast is a microorganism that ferments sugars to produce alcohol and carbon dioxide, making it the correct match.

Glycolysis → b (Glucose is converted into pyruvic acid)

· Glycolysis is the process in which glucose is broken down into pyruvic acid, releasing ATP.

Pyruvic acid → a (Intermediate substance in the breakdown of glucose)

· Pyruvic acid is an intermediate compound formed at the end of glycolysis and used in further metabolic pathways.
questions.solution_hi:
ग्लूकोज → d (श्वसन हेतु सर्वश्रेष्ठ कार्बनिक सब्सट्रेट)

• ग्लूकोज कोशिकीय श्वसन हेतु प्राथमिक ऊर्जा स्रोत है, जो इसे सर्वश्रेष्ठ कार्बनिक सब्सट्रेट बनाता है।

यीस्ट → c (किण्वन प्रक्रिया हेतु पोषक तत्वों का उपयोग करता है)

questions.q_en: What happens to the guard cells when water flows into them?
questions.solution_en: When water flows into the guard cells, they become turgid and swell, which leads to the opening of stomatal pores, allowing for the exchange of gases and transpiration in plants.
questions.solution_hi: जब पानी रक्षक कोशिकाओं में प्रवाहित होता है, तो वे स्फीत होकर फूल जाती हैं, जिससे रंध्रों का खुलना होता है, जो पौधों में गैस विनिमय व वाष्पोत्सर्जन की अनुमति देता है।

questions.q_en:
Which of following pair of plastids - thing stored is NOT correct?

I. Amyloplasts - oils and fats

II. Aleuroplasts - carbohydrates
questions.solution_en:
Amyloplasts are responsible for storing starch (carbohydrates), not oils and fats.

Aleuroplasts, on the other hand, are responsible for storing proteins but not carbohydrates.

Hence, neither statement I nor II is correct.
questions.solution_hi:
एमाइलोप्लास्ट स्टार्च (कार्बोहाइड्रेट) संग्रहीत करने हेतु उत्तरदायी हैं, तेल व वसा नहीं।

एल्युरोप्लास्ट, दूसरी ओर, प्रोटीन संग्रहीत करने हेतु उत्तरदायी हैं परंतु कार्बोहाइड्रेट नहीं।

अतः, न तो कथन I न ही II सही है।

questions.q_en: Which of the following causes enlargement and extension growth of cells?
questions.solution_en:
Turgor pressure refers to the pressure exerted by the cell membrane against the cell wall in plant cells, due to the water entering the cell. This pressure helps in the enlargement and extension of plant cells, as it maintains the rigidity and turgidity of the cell, which is necessary for cell growth.

Brief explanation of the other options:

· Imbibition: This is the process by which water is absorbed by solid particles, such as seeds or dry tissues, but it is not the primary cause of cell enlargement.

· Pressure potential: This is the potential energy due to pressure exerted on water within a cell, and although related to turgor, it is not directly responsible for cell growth.

· Osmotic pressure: This is the pressure exerted by water when it moves from a region of lower solute concentration to one of higher solute concentration. While it contributes to water uptake, it does not directly cause cell enlargement.
questions.solution_hi: स्फीति दाब (Turgor pressure) पादप कोशिकाओं में कोशिका झिल्ली द्वारा कोशिका भित्ति के विरुद्ध लगाए गए दबाव को संदर्भित करता है, जो कोशिका में पानी के प्रवेश के कारण होता है। यह दबाव पादप कोशिकाओं के विस्तार व वृद्धि में मदद करता है, क्योंकि यह कोशिका की कठोरता व स्फीति बनाए रखता है।

questions.q_en: What is the yellow dust present in the middle of a flower called?
questions.solution_en: The yellow dust present in the middle of a flower is called Pollen. Pollen is essential for sexual reproduction of flowering plants and plants that produce cones. Each pollen grain contains male gametes necessary for fertilisation. The scientific study of living and fossilised pollen grains is known as palynology. The male part of flowering plants is the stamen.
questions.solution_hi: फूल के बीच में मौजूद पीली धूल को पराग कहा जाता है। पराग पुष्पीय पौधों व शंकु उत्पन्न करने वाले पौधों के लैंगिक प्रजनन हेतु आवश्यक है। प्रत्येक पराग कण में निषेचन हेतु आवश्यक नर युग्मक होते हैं। जीवित व जीवाश्म पराग कणों के वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन को पराग विज्ञान (palynology) कहा जाता है।

questions.q_en: In which of the following plants do roots arise from parts of a plant other than the radicle?
questions.solution_en:
· Adventitious roots arise from parts of a plant other than the radicle (e.g., stems, leaves).

· Radicle: The embryonic root (first root) of a plant.

· Monstera: Develops aerial adventitious roots from its stems, which help it climb and absorb moisture (common in climbers/epiphytes).

· Other options:

o Turnip & Mustard: Have taproot systems (originating from the radicle).

o Maize: Has fibrous roots (also radicle-derived, though short-lived).
questions.solution_hi:
• अपस्थानिक (Adventitious) जड़ें मूलांकुर के अतिरिक्त पौधे के अन्य भागों (जैसे तना, पत्तियाँ) से निकलती हैं।

• मूलांकुर: पौधे की भ्रूणीय जड़ (पहली जड़)।

• मॉन्स्टेरा: अपने तनों से वायवीय अपस्थानिक जड़ें विकसित करता है, जो इसे चढ़ने व नमी अवशोषित करने में मदद करती हैं।

questions.q_en: The loss of water in the form of water droplets from leaves of plants is called _____
questions.solution_en:
Guttation is the process where water droplets are excreted from the edges of leaves, typically during the night or in the early morning.

· It occurs when the soil moisture is high, and root pressure forces water out through small openings called hydathodes.

· This happens when transpiration is low, unlike normal water loss through stomata (which occurs via transpiration).

Difference between Guttation and Transpiration:

FeatureGuttationTranspiration
Type of water lossLiquid (water droplets)Vapor
TimeNight or early morningDaytime
CauseRoot pressureEvaporation due to heat
OpeningsHydathodesStomata

Plants like banana, tomato, and grass commonly exhibit guttation.

questions.q_en: Identify the element that helps to trap light energy that is essential for photosynthesis.
questions.solution_en: Carotenoids are ubiquitous and essential pigments in photosynthesis. They absorb in the blue-green region of the solar spectrum and transfer the absorbed energy to (bacterio) chlorophylls, and so expand the wavelength range of light that is able to drive photosynthesis. This is an example of singlet-singlet energy transfer, and so carotenoids serve to enhance the overall efficiency of photosynthetic light reactions. Carotenoids also act to protect photosynthetic organisms from the harmful effects of excess exposure to light.
questions.solution_hi: कैरोटीनॉइड सर्वव्यापी व प्रकाश संश्लेषण में आवश्यक वर्णक हैं। ये सौर स्पेक्ट्रम के नीले-हरे क्षेत्र में अवशोषित करते हैं व अवशोषित ऊर्जा को (बैक्टीरियो) क्लोरोफिल में स्थानांतरित करते हैं, इस प्रकार प्रकाश संश्लेषण चलाने में सक्षम प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्ध्य सीमा को विस्तारित करते हैं।

questions.q_en: What is the reason for the similar size of the vascular bundle in monocot leaves?
questions.solution_en:
Monocot leaves have parallel venation, which results in similar-sized vascular bundles.

Key Points:

· Characteristic of monocot plant leaves

· Veins run parallel to each other

· Consistent vein structure throughout the leaf

· Examples include grass, corn, and palm leaves

· Differs from net or reticulate venation in dicot plants

· Reflects the fundamental structural differences between monocot and dicot plants

· Important in plant classification and identification
